Matt — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers below, plus I attached an initial SKU mapping to show how we usually normalize.

1) Invoice cutoff: we can support a fixed monthly cutoff (default is EOW rolling), so day-of-month 5pm PT is OK for a private-offer account — we'll pin that in billing ops and the PO. Note that any late adjustments after cutoff will be reflected as a separate correction invoice in the next cycle.

2) Reseller share across consolidated SKUs: we calculate the reseller share on net recognized revenue for the consolidated SKU, proportionally attributing historical usage from the legacy SKUs during the trailing lookback window (typically 30 days unless you request 90-day smoothing). See the attached mapping for a simple example.

Evidence: we typically require (a) signed PO, (b) monthly invoices showing usage, (c) reseller invoice/commission claim if partner is requesting payout. You can bundle these into one packet — a single PDF per quarter works fine.

Next steps: if Matt confirms 30-day smoothing and the 5pm PT cutoff, I will draft the billing clause and share a quick one-page operational checklist.

Evelyn / Matt — quick note on the math and evidence chain.

Reseller-share calc (summary):
- For consolidated SKU, compute net revenue per legacy SKU for the lookback period (usage * unit price less discounts).
- Sum net revenue across legacy SKUs mapped to consolidated SKU to get consolidated net revenue.
- Reseller share = consolidated net revenue * agreed-reseller-percentage.

Edge cases: if a legacy SKU had one-off credits or an implementation coupon, those get excluded from the numerator and reconciled separately (we show them as "adjustments" on the correction invoice).

Attached is a simple CSV that mirrors how finance will ingest the numbers; format: legacy_sku, usage_units, unit_price, discounts, net_revenue. If CloudSight can provide a CSV export from your usage portal, we can run a preflight and surface any gaps.

Lookback window: recommend 30 days by default; 90 days only if CloudSight expects significant month-to-month variability. 30 days is easier for cashflow modeling for partners.
